paper.title: Sub-Kelvin Stereodynamics of the Ne(3P2) + N2 Reaction
paper.affiliation: Institute for Chemical Sciences and Engineering, Ecole Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne (EPFL), 1015 Lausanne, Switzerland

research.objective: Experimental study of low-energy stereodynamics of the Ne(3P2) + N2 reaction, measuring branching between Penning ionization (PI) and associative ionization (AI) as a function of neon orientation and collision energy.
research.method: Merged beam technique with supersonic expansions of state-purified metastable Ne(3P2) and N2, combined with magnetic orientation control using solenoid magnets. Velocity control via valve temperature and seeding ratio yields collision energies from 60 mK to 700 K.
key_findings: Loss of ability to orient Ne below ≈100 K due to dynamic reorientation.
Associative ionization products Ne-N2+ predissociate with 30%–60% probability.
AI is entirely due to reactions of the Ω = 2 state, where the singly occupied p orbital of Ne* is oriented along the interatomic axis.
Steric effect pronounced above 100 K, absent below 10 K.
Local reduction in predissociation probability around 470 K tentatively assigned to a vibrational Feshbach resonance.

Ne*.mJ: magnetic quantum numbers (polarized via magnetic guide)
Ne*.Omega: Projection of J on interatomic axis: Ω = 0, 1, 2

quantum_numbers.mJ: Magnetic quantum number in lab frame
quantum_numbers.Omega: Projection of J on interparticle axis (Ω = 0, 1, 2)

theory.framework: Merged beam technique with magnetic orientation control. Wigner D-matrices transform measured mJ populations to molecular-frame Ω populations. Reaction cross sections expressed as I_AI,PI ∝ Σ_Ω p(Ω) σ_AI,PI(Ω).

potentials.interaction: Anisotropic Ne*-N2 potential; similar to Ne*-Ar potential [37]. Dynamic reorientation occurs when interatomic force overcomes magnetic orientation force.
potentials.expansion: Not explicitly given; referenced to Baudon et al. [37]

models.predissociation: Eq. (4): I_N2+(θ_kB, E_coll) = w(E_coll) I_NeN2+(θ_kB, E_coll) + I_PI(E_coll), where w is predissociation fraction.
models.reactivity: Eq. (5): R(θ_kB) = I_AI / I_PI = [I_NeN2+ + w I_NeN2+] / [I_N2+ - w I_NeN2+]. Below 30 K: R_lowE = I_NeN2+ / I_N2+.

approximations: PI is angle-independent; AI is angle-dependent and requires Ω=2.
Predissociation fraction w and direct PI signal I_PI do not depend on magnetic field direction but can vary with collision energy.
N2 rotational temperature ~20 K makes molecule effectively isotropic.

methods: Least-squares fit of Eq. (4) to raw angle-dependent ion yields to extract w(E_coll) and I_PI(E_coll).
Fit of measured reactivity R to I_AI/I_PI to extract Ω-specific ratios σ_Ω^AI / σ_Ω^PI.
Wigner D-matrix transformation from lab-frame mJ populations to molecular-frame Ω populations.

parameters.magnetic_field: Two pairs of solenoid magnets at 90° for arbitrary field direction

measured_quantities.conditions: As function of θ_kB and E_coll

measured_quantities.conditions: As function of θ_kB and E_coll

measured_quantities.conditions: Ratio of max to min reactivity vs θ_kB

main_findings: Above 30 K: AI/PI ratio strongly depends on θ_kB, oscillating between PI-dominated and AI-dominated; nearly independent of collision energy.
Below 30 K: Reactivity becomes independent of θ_kB (dynamic reorientation).
Ω = 2: AI reactivity ~2.5 at high E, drops to ~0.6 below 30 K. AI exclusively from Ω=2 above 30 K.
Ω = 0, 1: AI reactivity nearly zero at high E, rises to ~0.5 below 30 K.
Below 30 K: AI efficiency lower than PI for all Ω.
Steric effect (R(90°)/R(180°)) pronounced above 100 K, absent below 10 K.
Predissociation probability P_pd = 30%–60% over entire range, slight downward trend with decreasing E_coll.
Local minimum in P_pd at ~470 K coincides with v+ = 4 vibrational state of N2+ (tentative vibrational Feshbach resonance).
Dynamic reorientation threshold similar for Ne*+Ar and Ne*+N2 (~30 K), explained by similar interaction potentials.

quantitative_values.reorientation_threshold: ≈30 K (loss of steric control), ≈100 K (onset of reorientation)

comparisons.Ne*+Ar: Similar reorientation threshold (~30 K), but Ne*+Ar shows some AI from Ω=0,1 at high E, while Ne*+N2 shows none.

Fig4.content: Ω-resolved reactivities and steric effect quantification

experimental: Below 30 K, cannot extract predissociation information because reactivity is independent of θ_kB.
At lowest collision energies (pink shaded region in Fig. 4d), longitudinal relative velocities become comparable to transverse velocity spread, preventing orientational control.
N2 rotational temperature (~20 K) leaves population in rotationally excited states, making molecule effectively isotropic and masking anisotropy of Ne*-N2 potential.
Depolarization occurs between magnetic guide exit and interaction zone (30 cm), complicating polarization analysis.
theoretical: Model assumes PI is angle-independent and AI requires Ω=2; validity only confirmed above 30 K.
Tentative assignment of 470 K feature to vibrational Feshbach resonance requires confirmation via state-resolved detection and theoretical calculations.
Predissociation dynamics not fully characterized; long-lived states suppressing predissociation proposed but not verified [35].
